title: 7.5 A 353mW 112Gb/s Discrete Multitone Wireline Receiver Datapath with Time-Based ADC in 5nm FinFET
problem: High-speed >100Gb/s wireline receivers using traditional PAM-4 designs with large feed-forward equalizers (FFE) and decision-feedback equalizers (DFE) face exponentially increasing complexity as ISI cursors grow, and struggle with channel ripples/notches.
motivation: Server interconnect bandwidth demands push data rates beyond 112Gb/s, but traditional PAM-4 FFE+DFE+MLSE architectures become power and area prohibitive; complex channel responses with ripples limit equalization performance.
method: This receiver divides the incoming signal into many frequency bands (discrete multitone or DMT) and equalizes each band separately. A time-based ADC converts the analog signal to digital form by measuring how fast signals cross a threshold, rather than measuring voltage directly. Within each band, the receiver applies equalization and uses MLSE—an algorithm that picks the most likely transmitted sequence given what was actually received—to decode the data. This design sidesteps the fundamental problem with traditional PAM-4 approaches: they require massive numbers of equalizer stages (FFE taps) and face timing constraints in feedback paths (DFE), both of which become impractical above 100 Gb/s.
key_novelty: Discrete multitone (DMT) modulation with time-based ADC avoids the exponentially growing complexity of large equalizer stages (FFE and DFE) that traditional PAM-4 designs require at high speeds above 100 Gb/s.
contributions: Discrete multitone modulation for wireline receiver
limitations: Abstract-only; bit error rate, channel reach, area breakdown, ADC linearity, tone spacing, and comparison with PAM-4 alternatives not discussed.
primary_theme: DMT receiver for high-speed complex-channel wireline transmission
